audit_findings.title: The cash bridge is unreconciled and may double-count post-anchor cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $158.572 million bridge cash, equal to 87.1% of $182.0 million base equity value; 2026 first-half cash increase was $6.415 million and reported FCF was $10.251 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash is added in the equity bridge, while post-FY2025 operating cash may also be represented in the first projected DCF period; offering shares affect the per-share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had available cash and cash equivalents of $ 43,557 , an increase of $ 7,053 from $ 36,504 as of December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The $158.572 million amount does arithmetically reconcile to $49.972 million of June 30 cash plus $108.6 million of net offering proceeds. However, the DCF is anchored at FY2025, so using post-offering cash without a stub-period adjustment may count 2026 operating cash both in the bridge and in projected owner earnings. Because cash supplies most of the base equity value, even a partial timing error is capable of affecting the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a December 31, 2025-to-August 7, 2026 cash roll-forward, identify operating versus financing movements, use net offering proceeds, deduct any offering liabilities, align the DCF start date through a stub-period rerun, and use the same-date fully diluted share count.

audit_findings.title: Acquired-intangible payables may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.524 million at December 31, 2025, comprising $0.704 million current and $0.820 million noncurrent; $0.086 per fully diluted share and 0.84% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid acquisition consideration not already deducted through owner earnings should be deducted as a debt-like claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, noncurrent portion of payables related to acquired intangible assets of $ 820 were included in other noncurrent liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates an outstanding $1.524 million claim at FY2025, but the June balance-sheet captions indicate liabilities subsequently declined. Even deducting the entire filed FY2025 amount would reduce base value from $10.33 to about $10.24 per share and would not change the conclusion relative to the $76.14 market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30 and August 7 current and noncurrent acquired-intangible payable balances and confirm whether the purchase cash cost was already included in owner earnings; deduct any unreconciled balance, without otherwise changing the conclusion.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance software investment may be misclassified
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 capitalized cash costs of $10.593 million, 6.2 times the $1.7 million OE anchor; an additional $1.599 million of SBC was capitalized
audit_findings.mechanism: The maintenance portion of capitalized internal-use software is an owner-earnings deduction; treating maintenance as growth overstates OE, while treating expansion projects as maintenance understates OE. Capitalized SBC also interacts with the diluted-share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: In accordance with ASC 350-40, “Software—internal use software,” we capitalize eligible costs, including personnel-related expenses, share-based compensation, and travel expenses incurred by relevant employees, and other directly attributable costs incurred during the application development stage.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed capitalized spending is many times the valuation anchor, making the maintenance-versus-growth classification decisive. The accounting policy establishes capitalization but does not establish the economic maintenance share, so there is no demonstrated directional error, yet plausible reclassification can materially alter sustainable OE.
audit_findings.action: Trace FY2025 and 2026 capitalized costs by project and classify maintenance of functionality, ingestion, security, certifications and competitiveness separately from incremental products or capacity; reconcile capitalized SBC to share dilution and rerun OE under documented maintenance cases.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may not contain a full run-rate cloud commitment
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.0 million annual minimum; a simple eight-to-twelve-month annualization difference is $1.0 million, equal to 58.8% of the $1.7 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The recurring cloud cost reduces OE either through operating expense or through the maintenance portion of capitalized software spending.
audit_findings.evidence: The agreement includes a minimum annual purchase commitment of $ 3.0 million, beginning May 1, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing proves a recurring annual minimum beginning May 1, 2025, but does not disclose how much of the FY2025 cost entered expense, capitalization or the OE calculation. The computed $1.0 million annualization gap is not a demonstrated omission, but its scale relative to the anchor makes the issue capable of changing operating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile vendor invoices and commitment utilization for FY2025 and 2026 between expense and capitalized software, identify unused minimum payments, and rerun OE with a full-year recurring cost while preventing duplication with maintenance capex.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 taxes may not represent the sustainable common-equity burden
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 tax expense was $1.404 million at 10%; applying the disclosed 26% combined statutory rate to $14.558 million of pretax income gives $3.785 million, a computed $2.381 million increase; first-half 2026 effective rate was 24%
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash-tax normalization reduces forecast OE and terminal value; realizable tax attributes may separately affect near-term taxes or the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in income tax expense was primarily driven by a decrease in the effective tax rate to 10% for the year ended December 31, 2025 from 25% in 2024, partially offset by higher pre-tax income.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2026 effective rate of 24% demonstrates that FY2025's 10% rate was not a stable run rate. The computed normalization difference exceeds the $1.7 million anchor, so retaining the FY2025 tax benefit into the perpetual forecast could materially overstate value, although NOLs and credits may defer part of the burden.
audit_findings.action: Build an annual cash-tax schedule using the filed NOLs, credits, deferred-tax balances and expected SBC benefits; normalize the terminal tax rate, recognize temporary shelters only for their supported duration, and rerun the DCF.

audit_findings.title: The Daniel’s Law exposure may exceed insurance and recorded costs
audit_findings.mechanism: An uninsured deductible, excluded loss or award above policy limits would be a cash claim in the equity bridge; recurring defense costs would reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As such, the Company anticipates that the insurer will cover defense costs and any potential liability, subject to policy limits and customary exclusions.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing confirms that the claim is within insurance coverage, reports no trial date and provides no accrued or reasonably estimable uninsured loss. The possibility remains, but the record does not demonstrate a present valuation adjustment or quantify exposure; it should be monitored as the litigation and coverage position develop.
audit_findings.action: Monitor court developments and obtain policy limits, deductibles, exclusions and reservation-of-rights correspondence; rerun the bridge or OE only when an uninsured amount becomes filed, accrued or otherwise supportably estimable.
